cards.text: Isaiah the prophet brings a message about Bel and Nebo, gods of Babylon. Bel crouches and Nebo cowers. Friend, these gods are supposed to be in CHARGE, and somebody's hauling them around like a couch on moving day.

cards.question: Somebody has to haul Bel and Nebo's idols around. Who is it?

cards.text: You pray to a god, friend, and your god needs a RIDE, a heavy load on a tired animal. And the gods just cower and crouch together.

cards.question: Bel and Nebo are able to relieve the burden.
Bel and Nebo can't relieve the burden, and Isaiah says the gods themselves go into ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to the house of Jacob, all who are left of the house of Israel. Hold on to your hat, friend. Mine's so tall I need both sides of the mustache.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He has done for the house of Jacob since birth?
The LORD tells the house of Jacob that His care for them will stop once they grow old.

cards.text: He'll bear them up even when they turn gray. Friend, MY edges went soft with age, and I got slid into a junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD promises to carry Israel, sustain them and deliver them. What does He say He has already done for them?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike?" Friend, that's a SHORT list: the LORD on one side, and on the other side a gold statue that needs a cow to get to work.
Then He shows what people do: pour out bags of gold, weigh out silver on scales and hire a goldsmith. Mother Miller got me for a quarter, friend, and these folks are emptying whole BAGS.

cards.question: The goldsmith shapes the gold into a ___ so the people can bow down and worship.

cards.text: Then they lift it to their shoulders and carry it along. Another god that needs a RIDE.

cards.question: Once the people set their gold god down in its place, it never ___.

cards.text: Not budging from one spot? I did that for YEARS in a junk drawer, and nobody ever prayed to ME. But these people cry out to theirs.

cards.question: When the people cry out to their gold god, it answers and saves them from their troubles.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out to transgressors: remember this, take it to heart and be brave. Remember what happened long ago, friend, and I don't mean where you left your keys.

cards.question: As He tells them to remember what happened long ago, the LORD says there are other gods like Him.

cards.text: The LORD says He declares the end from the beginning. Friend, I can't even tell you how a batch turns out until the timer goes off.

cards.question: The LORD declares the end from the beginning, and He says His purpose will ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He's summoning someone from the east. He doesn't send a memo, friend. He paints a PICTURE.

cards.question: What picture does the LORD use for the one He summons from the east?

cards.text: He calls him a man for His purpose. From a far-off land, friend. I get winded hopping my gold base from one oven to the next.

cards.question: The LORD says His plan for the man from the east might not come to pass.

cards.text: The LORD says, "Listen to Me," and calls them stubborn people, far removed from righteousness. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer sure nobody would need me again, so I KNOW stubborn.

cards.question: The people are far removed from righteousness. What does the LORD say He is doing with His righteousness?
The LORD says His salvation will not be delayed, and He will grant salvation to ___.

cards.text: And He'll adorn Israel with His splendor. Friend, I spent years covered in dust. SPLENDOR is a serious upgrade.

findings.problem: The opening card identifies Isaiah and introduces Bel and Nebo, but it never says whom Isaiah's message is addressed to.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards gives the baker a basis to infer captivity. The blank simply asks for an unseen word from verse 2 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences, exceeding the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer falls is too close to moves and is arguably correct: an idol that stands without budging could reasonably be said never to fall.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
